findings.title: Build breaks if English source file is missing
findings.body: In `verifySafeHtml()`, when no English file is found at the computed path (e.g. for any translation file in `resources-community/...` whose corresponding `resources/.../messages_en.properties` does not exist), the code wraps the `FileNotFoundException` from `new FileInputStream(englishFile)` into a `RuntimeException`, which propagates out of `verify()` and aborts the Maven build. The English lookup should be best-effort: either skip the HTML/anchor checks, fall back to treating the translation as the source of truth, or at minimum record a non-fatal message in the returned list. Currently any new language that lacks a committed English counterpart (or any test fixture that only ships `_xx.properties`) will crash the verifier.

findings.title: Typo in method name `santizeAnchors`
findings.body: The method is named `santizeAnchors` (missing the 'i' in 'sanitize'). The misspelling is also propagated to the only call site, so it does not affect behavior. It should be renamed to `sanitizeAnchors` so it reads correctly, matches the surrounding `verifySafeHtml()` naming style, and can be found by IDEs/refactoring tools.

findings.title: HTML_TAGS pattern is case-sensitive, mismatching the sanitizer
findings.body:
The pattern `HTML_TAGS = Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")` only matches lowercase HTML tag names. The OWASP sanitizer used right after is case-insensitive (HTML tags are not case sensitive in the spec). Consequence: `containsHtml(englishValue)` returns `false` for English values containing only uppercase tags (e.g. ``/``), so `POLICY_NO_HTML` is selected even though the English string actually has HTML. For an English-only check this does not matter (the sanitizer still strips the tags), but the choice of policy governs whether `
`, `

`, ``, `` are allowed in the translation. If English ever ships uppercase variants, the corresponding translations would be incorrectly forced through the no-HTML policy. The regex should be case-insensitive (e.g. `]*>` with `Pattern.CASE_INSENSITIVE`).

findings.title: Policy factories and regex are non-static instance fields
findings.body: `POLICY_SOME_HTML`, `POLICY_NO_HTML`, and `HTML_TAGS` are instance fields even though they do not depend on any instance state and are constructed purely from constants. A new `PolicyFactory` and `Pattern` is allocated for every `VerifyMessageProperties` instance (i.e. once per message file). They should be `private static final` so they are compiled once and shared across all verifications, which is both faster and clearer about their immutability.

findings.title: santizeAnchors couples mutable value with matcher bound to original
findings.body: `santizeAnchors` creates `matcher = ANCHOR_PATTERN.matcher(value)` once before the loop, then inside the loop assigns `value = value.replaceFirst(...)`. The `matcher` keeps operating on the *original* string, but `replaceFirst` is invoked on the *mutated* `value`. In the common case the anchor tags appear in the same order in both strings and the algorithm accidentally works, but this is fragile: e.g. if the translation contains the same anchor tag multiple times or if `replaceFirst` removes a substring that affects positions of subsequent matches, `matcher.find()` will read positions in the original while `value` has shifted, leading to mismatches between `matcher.group()` and the substring actually being replaced. The matcher should be rebuilt from `value` after each replacement, or the anchors should be collected first and then stripped from the value.

findings.title: No test for missing English source file
findings.body: The new test suite only covers cases where an English file is present (`changedAnchor_en.properties`, `noHtml_en.properties`, `illegalHtmlTag_en.properties`, `duplicateKeys_en.properties`). The branch where `new FileInputStream(englishFile)` throws FileNotFoundException (the `catch (IOException e) { throw new RuntimeException(...) }` block at line 79) has no coverage. Add a fixture that ships only a translation without an English counterpart and assert either that `verify()` returns a graceful message in the list, or (if RuntimeException is intentional) document and assert that behavior, so future refactors do not silently change it.

findings.title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 was replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The Lithuanian translation for `loginTotpStep1` was changed from a proper Lithuanian sentence with embedded `<a>` tags to the Italian string `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`. The English source is `Install one of the following applications on your mobile:`. Users with Lithuanian locale now see an Italian sentence in the login UI instead of Lithuanian. This appears to be a copy/paste error from the Czech/Slovak/Swedish translations done in this PR. The original Lithuanian wording or a proper new Lithuanian translation should be used.

findings.title: Lithuanian account totpStep1 was replaced with Italian text
findings.body: Same issue as in the login theme: the Lithuanian `totpStep1` was changed to the Italian `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`. Lithuanian users of the account theme will see Italian text instead of Lithuanian. Replace with a proper Lithuanian translation (the previous Lithuanian text was removed because it contained `<a>` tags, but it should have been rewritten in Lithuanian, not in Italian).

findings.title: Test fixture ends without a trailing newline
findings.body: Several new test fixtures under `misc/theme-verifier/src/test/resources/` (`changedAnchor_de.properties`, `changedAnchor_en.properties`, `illegalHtmlTag_en.properties`, `noHtml_de.properties`, `noHtml_en.properties`) are missing the final newline. Some tooling (and `PropertyResourceBundle` / `Files.readString` consumers in stricter environments) behave inconsistently for files not terminated by a newline. Add a trailing newline to keep with POSIX text-file conventions.
